stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether the color of a drink affects the ability to identify its flavor. They recruited 70 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition tasted ten fruit drinks whose colors did not match their flavors. Participants in the other condition tasted the same ten drinks with matching colors. The researchers then recorded the number of flavors out of ten that each participant named correctly.

Researchers investigated whether the presence of other people slows the reporting of an emergency. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were filling in a form in a room with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants in the other condition were filling in the form alone when smoke began to enter the room. The researchers then recorded the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

Researchers investigated whether caffeine improves attention. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition drank coffee containing 200 milligrams of caffeine. Participants in the other condition drank decaffeinated coffee that tasted the same. The researchers then recorded the number of targets that each participant correctly detected in a ten-minute computer task.

Researchers investigated whether an expected reward reduces children's later interest in drawing. They recruited 60 preschool children who enjoyed drawing and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were promised a certificate for drawing and received it. Children in the other condition drew with no reward mentioned. The researchers then recorded the number of minutes that each child chose to spend drawing during free time one week later.
Researchers collected data from 450 adults. For each one, they recorded optimism score and the number of days of illness in a year. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.30.

Researchers investigated whether mindfulness meditation lowers stress. They recruited 84 office workers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition practiced mindfulness meditation for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition listened to an audiobook for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded the level of the stress hormone cortisol in a saliva sample from each participant.

Researchers investigated whether praise increases hand raising in class. They recruited 50 second-grade students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were praised by the teacher each time they raised a hand before speaking. Children in the other condition received no special response when they raised a hand. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child raised a hand during one week.

Researchers collected data from 350 adults. For each one, they recorded the number of stressful life events in the past year and the number of colds in the past year. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.33.

Researchers investigated whether agreeing to a small request makes people more likely to agree to a large one. They recruited 120 homeowners and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Homeowners in one condition were first asked to sign a road-safety petition and two weeks later were asked to put a large sign in their garden. Homeowners in the other condition were only asked to put the large sign in their garden. The researchers then recorded the percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign.

Researchers investigated whether a new drug reduces anxiety. They recruited 150 adults diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition took the new drug every day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition took a placebo pill that looked identical every day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard anxiety questionnaire after eight weeks.

Researchers investigated whether a phone conversation reduces what drivers notice. They recruited 64 licensed drivers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a hands-free phone conversation while using a driving simulator. Participants in the other condition used the driving simulator without a phone. The researchers then recorded the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.01.

rows.group: The group that talked on the phone
The group that drove without a phone

stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 300 fifth-grade students. For each one, they recorded working memory span and reading comprehension score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.52.

Researchers collected data from 600 university students. For each one, they recorded conscientiousness score on a personality inventory and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.35.

Researchers collected data from 400 high school students. For each one, they recorded the average number of hours slept per night and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.45.

Researchers investigated whether a smiling expression makes cartoons seem funnier. They recruited 90 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a pen between their teeth, which produces a smile. Participants in the other condition held a pen between their lips, which prevents a smile. The researchers then recorded the rating from 1 to 10 that each participant gave to a set of cartoons. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.01.

rows.group: The group that held the pen between the teeth
The group that held the pen between the lips

stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 1,000 students. For each one, they recorded intelligence test score at age 11 and average school grade at age 16. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.60.
Researchers collected data from 500 adults aged 20 to 80. For each one, they recorded age and score on a timed reasoning test. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.55.
Researchers collected data from 250 adults. For each one, they recorded resting heart rate and self-rated anxiety. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.38.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether guided hints help children learn to solve puzzles. They hypothesized that help from an adult would affect problem-solving skill.

**Participants.** The sample was 64 five-year-old children, recruited from one city. Parents gave informed consent, each child gave assent, and the plan was approved by an institutional review board. Families could withdraw at any time.

**Method.** The children were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Children in one condition solved practice puzzles with hints from an adult that were gradually reduced. Children in the other condition solved the same practice puzzles alone. The researchers recorded the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help.

**Results.** The group that received hints: mean new puzzles solved (out of 10) = 7.2. The group that practiced alone: mean new puzzles solved (out of 10) = 4.6. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Which study methods lead to the best long-term learning?**

**Source A.** In an experiment, 90 students were randomly assigned to study 40 vocabulary words either in six ten-minute sessions on different days or in one sixty-minute session. One month later, the spaced group recalled a mean of 27 words and the single-session group a mean of 16 (p = 0.01).

**Source B.** In an experiment, 120 students read a passage and were randomly assigned either to take three practice quizzes or to reread the passage three times. On a test one week later, the quiz group scored a mean of 68 percent and the rereading group 49 percent (p = 0.01).

**Source C.** In a survey of 600 students, 71 percent said that rereading notes was their main study method, and most rated it as highly effective. Only 12 percent said that they regularly tested themselves.

questions.stem: After a stroke, a man can describe a person's nose and eyes but cannot recognize his own wife's face. Which condition does he have?

options.why: Dichromatism is a form of color vision deficiency in which one of the three types of cones does not work.
Monochromatism is a rare form of color blindness in which a person sees only shades of gray.
Correct. Prosopagnosia is the inability to recognize faces, even familiar ones, after brain damage.
The trichromatic theory is the theory that the retina has three types of color receptors, sensitive to red, green and blue.

questions.explanation: Prosopagnosia is the inability to recognize faces, even familiar ones, after brain damage.

questions.stem: A vending machine delivers a snack every time money is inserted. Which schedule of reinforcement is this?

options.why: A fixed-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after a set amount of time is reinforced.
A variable-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after an unpredictable amount of time is reinforced.
A variable-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after an unpredictable number of responses.
Correct. Continuous reinforcement is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced every time it occurs.

questions.explanation: Continuous reinforcement is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced every time it occurs.

questions.stem: Taking a tablet makes Lena's headache go away, so she is more likely to take a tablet next time. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Positive reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by adding a pleasant stimulus after it.
Correct. Negative reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus after it.
Positive punishment is the weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it.
Negative punishment is the weakening of a behavior by removing a pleasant stimulus after it.

questions.explanation: Negative reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus after it.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes cognitive-behavioral therapy?

options.text: The therapy that combines changing self-defeating thoughts with changing behavior
options.why: Correct. This is what cognitive-behavioral therapy means.

options.text: The pattern of negative thoughts about oneself, the world and the future that is found in depression
options.why: That describes the cognitive triad.

options.text: The confrontational cognitive therapy, developed by Ellis, that actively challenges a client's irrational beliefs
options.why: That describes rational emotive behavior therapy.

options.text: The technique of identifying irrational thoughts and replacing them with more realistic ones
options.why: That describes cognitive restructuring.

questions.explanation: Cognitive-behavioral therapy is the therapy that combines changing self-defeating thoughts with changing behavior.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: The mismatched drinks were served colder than the matching drinks
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

options.text: One group differed from the other in the color of the drinks
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

options.text: The two groups differed in flavor identification at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: Before taking part, each participant was told what the study would involve and what the risks were, and then agreed to take part. Which ethical guideline does this meet?

options.why: Debriefing happens after the study.
Correct. Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.
That is a research procedure, not an ethical guideline.
Confidentiality is keeping participants' data private.

questions.explanation: Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the identity status of a person who has made a commitment without exploring options?

options.why: Identity moratorium is the identity status of a person who is actively exploring options but has not yet made a commitment.
Identity diffusion is the identity status of a person who has neither explored options nor made a commitment.
Identity achievement is the identity status of a person who has explored options and made a commitment.
Correct. Identity foreclosure is the identity status of a person who has made a commitment without exploring options.

questions.explanation: Identity foreclosure is the identity status of a person who has made a commitment without exploring options.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the weakening of a conditioned response when the conditioned stimulus is repeatedly presented alone?

options.why: Spontaneous recovery is the reappearance of a weakened conditioned response after a rest period.
Acquisition is in classical conditioning, the first stage, in which the neutral stimulus is paired with the unconditioned stimulus and the response is learned.
Stimulus discrimination is the learned ability to respond to the conditioned stimulus but not to similar stimuli.
Correct. Extinction is the weakening of a conditioned response when the conditioned stimulus is repeatedly presented alone.

questions.explanation: Extinction is the weakening of a conditioned response when the conditioned stimulus is repeatedly presented alone.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a harmful agent, such as alcohol or a virus, that can damage an embryo or fetus?

options.why: Imprinting is the process by which some animals form a strong attachment to the first moving object they see.
Fine motor skills is the movements that use small muscles, such as grasping a crayon or buttoning a shirt.
Correct. A teratogen is a harmful agent, such as alcohol or a virus, that can damage an embryo or fetus.
The rooting reflex is a newborn's automatic turning of the head toward a touch on the cheek, to find food.

questions.explanation: A teratogen is a harmful agent, such as alcohol or a virus, that can damage an embryo or fetus.

questions.stem: Carl avoided fish after becoming ill only once. Learning that takes place after a single pairing is called which of the following?

options.why: A taste aversion is a learned dislike of a food that was followed by illness.
Biological preparedness is the inborn readiness to learn some associations, such as taste and nausea, more easily than others.
Habituation is the decrease in response to a stimulus that is presented over and over.
Correct. One-trial conditioning is learning that happens after a single pairing of two stimuli.

questions.explanation: One-trial conditioning is learning that happens after a single pairing of two stimuli.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a drug that reduces tension by depressing central nervous system activity and can be addictive?

options.why: Correct. An antianxiety drug is a drug that reduces tension by depressing central nervous system activity and can be addictive.
An antidepressant is a drug, such as an SSRI, that treats depression and anxiety by raising the availability of serotonin or norepinephrine.
Lithium is the mood-stabilizing drug used to treat bipolar disorder.
Tardive dyskinesia is the involuntary movements of the face and tongue that can result from long-term use of antipsychotic drugs.

questions.explanation: An antianxiety drug is a drug that reduces tension by depressing central nervous system activity and can be addictive.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the fight-or-flight response?

options.text: The response to stress in which the sympathetic nervous system prepares the body to attack or escape
options.why: Correct. This is what the fight-or-flight response means.

options.text: The response to stress of caring for others and seeking social support
options.why: That describes the tend-and-befriend response.

options.text: The field that studies how behavior, thoughts and emotions affect physical health and illness
options.why: That describes health psychology.

options.text: An event or situation that a person sees as threatening or challenging
options.why: That describes a stressor.

questions.explanation: The fight-or-flight response is the response to stress in which the sympathetic nervous system prepares the body to attack or escape.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the personality disorder marked by an excessive need to be taken care of and by clinging, submissive behavior?

options.why: Correct. Dependent personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an excessive need to be taken care of and by clinging, submissive behavior.
Antisocial personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by a lack of conscience and disregard for the rights of others.
Narcissistic personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an exaggerated sense of self-importance and a need for admiration.
Histrionic personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by excessive emotion and attention seeking.

questions.explanation: Dependent personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an excessive need to be taken care of and by clinging, submissive behavior.

questions.stem: A patient stands rigid in one position for several hours and does not respond to anyone. Which symptom is this?

options.why: Disorganized speech is the jumbled, illogical speech, sometimes called word salad, that is a symptom of schizophrenia.
A hallucination is a sensory experience, such as hearing voices, that occurs without any outside stimulus.
Correct. Catatonia is a disturbance of movement in which a person may remain motionless for hours or move without purpose.
Flat affect is a lack of emotional expression in the face and voice.

questions.explanation: Catatonia is a disturbance of movement in which a person may remain motionless for hours or move without purpose.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes proactive interference?

options.text: The disruption of new learning by older memories
options.why: Correct. This is what proactive interference means.

options.text: The temporary inability to retrieve a word that one is sure one knows
options.why: That describes the tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon.

options.text: The pattern in which memory fades quickly at first and then levels off
options.why: That describes the forgetting curve.

options.text: The disruption of older memories by new learning
options.why: That describes retroactive interference.

questions.explanation: Proactive interference is the disruption of new learning by older memories.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.

options.text: The group that drank caffeinated coffee
options.why: This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.
Only the comparison group is the control group.

options.text: The group that drank decaffeinated coffee
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes discontinuous development?

options.text: The view that development is a gradual, steady process, like a ramp
options.why: That describes continuous development.

options.text: The developmental question of how heredity and experience together shape a person
options.why: That describes nature and nurture.

options.text: The view that development happens in distinct stages, like a staircase
options.why: Correct. This is what discontinuous development means.

options.text: Research that follows the same people and retests them over a long period
options.why: That describes a longitudinal study.

questions.explanation: Discontinuous development is the view that development happens in distinct stages, like a staircase.

questions.stem: Students at one school say, 'People at that other school are all the same,' while describing their own classmates as varied individuals. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Cognitive dissonance is the discomfort a person feels when their actions and attitudes conflict, which motivates a change in one of them.
Confirmation bias is the tendency to search for and favor information that supports what one already believes.
Belief perseverance is the tendency to hold on to a belief even after the evidence for it has been discredited.
Correct. Out-group homogeneity bias is the tendency to see the members of other groups as all alike.

questions.explanation: Out-group homogeneity bias is the tendency to see the members of other groups as all alike.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: The children promised a certificate were given newer pens to draw with
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

options.text: The two groups differed in intrinsic motivation to draw at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

options.text: One group differed from the other in an expected reward
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the idea that schizophrenia involves excessive activity of the neurotransmitter dopamine?

options.why: Correct. The dopamine hypothesis is the idea that schizophrenia involves excessive activity of the neurotransmitter dopamine.
An acute onset is the sudden appearance of schizophrenia, often after stress, from which recovery is more likely.
A positive symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that adds an inappropriate behavior or experience, such as hallucinations.
A negative symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that takes away a normal behavior, such as emotional expression or motivation.

questions.explanation: The dopamine hypothesis is the idea that schizophrenia involves excessive activity of the neurotransmitter dopamine.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = +0.50. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: The relationship with the negative sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: A hiker sees a bear. Her heart pounds, her pupils widen and her digestion slows. Which part of the nervous system produced these changes?

options.why: Correct. The sympathetic nervous system is the division of the autonomic nervous system that arouses the body for fight or flight.
The autonomic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls glands and internal organs without conscious effort.
The somatic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls voluntary movement of the skeletal muscles.
The central nervous system is the brain and spinal cord.

questions.explanation: The sympathetic nervous system is the division of the autonomic nervous system that arouses the body for fight or flight.

questions.stem: After the study, the researchers explained its full purpose to every participant and answered their questions. What is this called?

options.why: Correct. Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.
A placebo is an inactive treatment.
Consent is obtained before the study.
Replication is repeating a study.

questions.explanation: Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a twin study?

options.text: The approach that explains behavior through natural selection of traits that helped ancestors survive and reproduce
options.why: That describes the evolutionary perspective.

options.text: The discredited movement that misused ideas about heredity to argue for selective breeding of humans
options.why: That describes eugenics.

options.text: Research that compares identical and fraternal twins to estimate the influence of heredity
options.why: Correct. This is what a twin study means.

options.text: The influence of environmental factors, such as upbringing and experience, on behavior and mental processes
options.why: That describes nurture.

questions.explanation: A twin study is research that compares identical and fraternal twins to estimate the influence of heredity.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes overconfidence?

options.text: The inaccuracy that arises when people describe their own behavior or feelings
options.why: That describes self-report bias.

options.text: The tendency to be more certain than correct about one's own judgments
options.why: Correct. This is what overconfidence means.

options.text: The tendency, after learning an outcome, to believe one would have predicted it
options.why: That describes hindsight bias.

options.text: The influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study
options.why: That describes experimenter bias.

questions.explanation: Overconfidence is the tendency to be more certain than correct about one's own judgments.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.why: This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.
Only the comparison group is the control group.

options.text: The group that received no special response
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.why: Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

options.text: The number of stressful life events in the past year
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.

options.text: The number of colds in the past year
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.
This is the statistic, not a variable.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: That is explaining the study to participants afterward.
That is an in-depth study of one individual.
That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as in classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning?

options.why: The unconditioned response is in classical conditioning, the natural, unlearned response to a stimulus.
The conditioned response is in classical conditioning, the learned response to a previously neutral stimulus.
Correct. The unconditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning.
The conditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the originally neutral stimulus that triggers a response after being paired with another stimulus.

questions.explanation: The unconditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning.

questions.stem: A therapist does not give advice; she listens with empathy and accepts whatever her client says, trusting the client to find his own answers. Which therapy is this?

options.why: Group therapy is the therapy in which several clients meet together with a therapist and benefit from each other's support.
Correct. Person-centered therapy is the humanistic therapy in which the therapist provides acceptance and empathy so that the client can grow.
Free association is the psychodynamic technique in which the client says whatever comes to mind.
Dream interpretation is the psychodynamic technique of analyzing dreams to uncover unconscious wishes and conflicts.

questions.explanation: Person-centered therapy is the humanistic therapy in which the therapist provides acceptance and empathy so that the client can grow.

questions.stem: Lights on a sign flash one after another, and viewers see a single light moving along the sign. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Color constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same color under different lighting.
Shape constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same shape even when the viewing angle changes.
Size constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same size even when its image on the retina changes.
Correct. Apparent movement is the perception of motion when a series of still images or lights is shown in quick succession.

questions.explanation: Apparent movement is the perception of motion when a series of still images or lights is shown in quick succession.

questions.stem: After a head injury, Amir can learn new things but cannot remember anything from the year before the accident. Which condition does he have?

options.why: Anterograde amnesia is the inability to form new memories after an injury or illness.
Infantile amnesia is the inability of adults to remember events from the first few years of life.
Correct. Retrograde amnesia is the loss of memories from before an injury or illness.
Alzheimer's disease is a progressive brain disease that destroys memory and then other mental abilities.

questions.explanation: Retrograde amnesia is the loss of memories from before an injury or illness.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as an explanation of behavior that points to the person's own traits or character?

options.why: The mere exposure effect is the tendency to like something more simply because we have encountered it repeatedly.
Correct. A dispositional attribution is an explanation of behavior that points to the person's own traits or character.
An internal locus of control is the belief that a person controls their own outcomes through their own actions.
A self-fulfilling prophecy is an expectation that leads a person to act in ways that make the expectation come true.

questions.explanation: A dispositional attribution is an explanation of behavior that points to the person's own traits or character.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes stereotype lift?

options.text: The belief that intelligence can be developed through effort and learning
options.why: That describes a growth mindset.

options.text: The boost in performance that comes from awareness that another group is negatively stereotyped
options.why: Correct. This is what stereotype lift means.

options.text: The worry about confirming a negative stereotype about one's group, which can lower performance
options.why: That describes stereotype threat.

options.text: The belief that intelligence is set and cannot be changed
options.why: That describes a fixed mindset.

questions.explanation: Stereotype lift is the boost in performance that comes from awareness that another group is negatively stereotyped.

questions.stem: The drug group had lower anxiety scores. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The type of pill and anxiety are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

options.text: The type of pill caused the difference in anxiety
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: The more hours children spend reading, the larger their vocabularies tend to be. Which kind of relationship is this?

options.why: A scatterplot is a graph in which each point shows one individual's values on two variables.
The third variable problem is the possibility that an unmeasured factor causes the relationship between two correlated variables.
A negative correlation is a relationship in which one variable rises as the other falls.
Correct. A positive correlation is a relationship in which two variables rise and fall together.

questions.explanation: A positive correlation is a relationship in which two variables rise and fall together.

questions.stem: A researcher gives one randomly chosen group a vitamin and another group a sugar pill, then compares their memory scores. Which research method is this?

options.why: Falsifiability is the quality of a claim that it could be shown to be wrong by evidence.
An operational definition is a statement of exactly how a variable is measured or manipulated in a study.
Correct. An experiment is the research method in which a researcher manipulates a variable and randomly assigns participants, which allows conclusions about cause and effect.
A survey is the research method of collecting self-reported attitudes or behaviors from a sample by asking questions.

questions.explanation: An experiment is the research method in which a researcher manipulates a variable and randomly assigns participants, which allows conclusions about cause and effect.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a specific learning disorder?

options.text: The eating disorder in which a person repeatedly eats very large amounts and feels distress, without purging afterward
options.why: That describes binge-eating disorder.

options.text: The eating disorder in which a person binges on food and then makes up for it by vomiting, fasting or excessive exercise
options.why: That describes bulimia nervosa.

options.text: The eating disorder in which a person restricts food to the point of being dangerously underweight, with an intense fear of gaining weight
options.why: That describes anorexia nervosa.

options.text: The neurodevelopmental disorder marked by persistent difficulty in reading, writing or math despite normal intelligence
options.why: Correct. This is what a specific learning disorder means.

questions.explanation: A specific learning disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by persistent difficulty in reading, writing or math despite normal intelligence.

questions.stem: A nine-year-old is asked whether she is willing to take part in a study after her parents have given permission. What is her agreement called?

options.why: Protection from harm is the requirement that researchers keep the physical and psychological risks to participants as low as possible.
Correct. Informed assent is the agreement of a minor to take part in a study, given in addition to a parent's consent.
Informed consent is the agreement of participants to take part after they have been told what a study involves.
An institutional review board is the committee that reviews research plans to make sure participants are treated ethically.

questions.explanation: Informed assent is the agreement of a minor to take part in a study, given in addition to a parent's consent.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant, so it is unlikely to be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

options.text: The two groups had the same average result
options.why: The table shows different averages.

options.text: The results prove that every individual in the first group differed from every individual in the second
options.why: The table reports group averages, not individual scores.

options.text: The difference between the groups is probably due to chance
options.why: A p value of 0.01 is below 0.05, so chance is an unlikely explanation.

questions.explanation: A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the second phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body stays highly aroused to cope with a continuing stressor?

options.why: The general adaptation syndrome is Selye's three-phase description of the body's response to long-term stress: alarm, resistance and exhaustion.
The alarm reaction is the first phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the sympathetic nervous system is suddenly activated.
Correct. The resistance phase is the second phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body stays highly aroused to cope with a continuing stressor.
The exhaustion phase is the third phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body's resources run out and illness becomes more likely.

questions.explanation: The resistance phase is the second phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body stays highly aroused to cope with a continuing stressor.

questions.stem: In psychodynamic theory, denial, projection and rationalization are all examples of which of the following?

options.why: The self-actualizing tendency is in humanistic theory, the inborn drive of people to grow and fulfill their potential.
The unconscious is in psychodynamic theory, the store of thoughts, wishes and memories that a person is not aware of but that still influences behavior.
Correct. A defense mechanism is in psychodynamic theory, a method the ego uses without awareness to reduce anxiety by distorting reality.
A projective test is a personality test, such as an inkblot test, that asks people to interpret unclear images in order to reveal hidden feelings.

questions.explanation: A defense mechanism is in psychodynamic theory, a method the ego uses without awareness to reduce anxiety by distorting reality.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes framing?

options.text: The activation, often without awareness, of certain associations that then influence perception or behavior
options.why: That describes priming.

options.text: The way the wording of an issue affects decisions and judgments
options.why: Correct. This is what framing means.

options.text: The mistaken belief that a random event is more likely because it has not happened recently
options.why: That describes the gambler's fallacy.

options.text: The judging of how likely something is by how easily examples come to mind
options.why: That describes the availability heuristic.

questions.explanation: Framing is the way the wording of an issue affects decisions and judgments.

questions.stem: At seventy, Mr. Park is slower than he used to be at solving unfamiliar logic puzzles. Which kind of intelligence has declined?

options.why: The zone of proximal development is the gap between what a learner can do alone and what the learner can do with help.
Correct. Fluid intelligence is the ability to reason quickly and abstractly, which tends to decline in older adulthood.
Crystallized intelligence is the accumulated knowledge and verbal skills that tend to increase with age.
Dementia is a serious decline in memory and thinking that interferes with daily life, most common in old age.

questions.explanation: Fluid intelligence is the ability to reason quickly and abstractly, which tends to decline in older adulthood.

questions.stem: Signals from the eyes, ears and skin pass through one structure that routes them to the correct areas of the cortex. Which structure is this?

options.why: Correct. The thalamus is the brain's sensory relay station, which directs incoming signals to the cortex.
The pituitary gland is the master gland of the endocrine system, which is controlled by the hypothalamus.
The medulla is the base of the brainstem, which controls heartbeat and breathing.
The reticular activating system is the network of neurons in the brainstem that controls arousal and alertness.

questions.explanation: The thalamus is the brain's sensory relay station, which directs incoming signals to the cortex.

questions.stem: If the data were shown on a scatterplot, what pattern would the points form?

options.why: Only a correlation of +1.00 or −1.00 gives a perfect line.

options.text: A shapeless cloud with no slope
options.why: That would show a correlation near zero.

options.text: A loose band that slopes upward from left to right
options.why: Correct. A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

options.text: A loose band that slopes downward from left to right
options.why: That would show a negative correlation.

questions.explanation: A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a procedure in which neither the participants nor the researchers who deal with them know who is in which condition?

options.why: The control group is the group in an experiment that does not receive the treatment and is used for comparison.
Effect size is the measure of how large the difference or relationship found in a study is.
Correct. A double-blind procedure is a procedure in which neither the participants nor the researchers who deal with them know who is in which condition.
The placebo effect is an improvement that results from a person's expectation of a treatment rather than from the treatment itself.

questions.explanation: A double-blind procedure is a procedure in which neither the participants nor the researchers who deal with them know who is in which condition.

questions.stem: An eight-year-old answers the questions that a typical ten-year-old can answer. On Binet's test, ten is the child's what?

options.why: Correct. Mental age is the level of performance typical of a certain chronological age on an intelligence test.
The Flynn effect is the steady rise in average intelligence test scores over the generations.
General intelligence is the single underlying mental ability that Spearman believed affects performance on all mental tasks.
Multiple intelligences is the theory that people have several independent kinds of intelligence, such as musical and interpersonal.

questions.explanation: Mental age is the level of performance typical of a certain chronological age on an intelligence test.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.

options.text: Conscientiousness score on a personality inventory
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.

options.text: The number of hours worked in a paid job
options.why: Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.
This is the statistic, not a variable.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: A one-year-old says 'milk' to mean 'I want some milk'. Which stage of language development is this?

options.why: Overgeneralization is the applying of a grammar rule too widely, as in 'goed' or 'mouses'.
Cooing is the vowel-like sounds, such as 'ooh', that infants make from about two months.
Telegraphic speech is the two-word stage in which a child uses mostly nouns and verbs, such as 'want juice'.
Correct. The one-word stage is the stage from about age 1 in which a child speaks mostly in single words.

questions.explanation: The one-word stage is the stage from about age 1 in which a child speaks mostly in single words.

questions.stem: Too little of one neurotransmitter is linked to the tremors of Parkinson's disease, and too much activity of it is linked to schizophrenia. Which neurotransmitter is this?

options.why: Endorphins is the neurotransmitters that reduce pain and increase pleasure.
Norepinephrine is the neurotransmitter that helps control alertness and arousal.
Correct. Dopamine is the neurotransmitter that influences movement, attention, and feelings of reward.
GABA is the brain's main inhibitory neurotransmitter.

questions.explanation: Dopamine is the neurotransmitter that influences movement, attention, and feelings of reward.

questions.stem: An advertisement for a car lists its safety ratings, fuel economy and repair costs. Which route to persuasion is it using?

options.why: Informational social influence is the influence that comes from a person's willingness to accept others' views as evidence about reality.
The door-in-the-face technique is the strategy of making a large request that will be refused so that a smaller request is more likely to be accepted.
Correct. The central route to persuasion is persuasion that works through evidence and logical arguments, which people think about carefully.
Normative social influence is the influence that comes from a person's desire to gain approval or avoid rejection.

questions.explanation: The central route to persuasion is persuasion that works through evidence and logical arguments, which people think about carefully.

questions.stem: To treat severe epilepsy, surgeons cut the fibers that carry messages between the left and right hemispheres. Which structure was cut?

options.why: Correct. The corpus callosum is the band of fibers that connects the two hemispheres of the brain.
The hypothalamus is the structure that regulates hunger, thirst, body temperature and sexual behavior and controls the pituitary gland.
The amygdala is the structure that processes fear and aggression.
The cerebral cortex is the wrinkled outer layer of the brain, which handles thinking, perception and voluntary movement.

questions.explanation: The corpus callosum is the band of fibers that connects the two hemispheres of the brain.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the part of working memory that briefly holds spoken and written words?

options.why: The central executive is the part of working memory that directs attention and coordinates the other parts.
Correct. The phonological loop is the part of working memory that briefly holds spoken and written words.
Long-term potentiation is the strengthening of the connections between neurons after repeated activation, which is the biological basis of memory.
The visuospatial sketchpad is the part of working memory that briefly holds images and spatial information.

questions.explanation: The phonological loop is the part of working memory that briefly holds spoken and written words.

questions.stem: What does the correlation show?

options.text: The first measure causes the second
options.why: A correlation does not show cause and effect.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with higher values of the second
options.why: Correct. A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with lower values of the second
options.why: That would be a negative correlation.
A correlation of zero would show no relationship.

questions.explanation: A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

questions.stem: While chatting at a crowded party, Deshawn suddenly notices his own name spoken across the room. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Selective attention is the focusing of awareness on one stimulus while ignoring others.
Change blindness is the failure to notice that something in the environment has changed.
Inattentional blindness is the failure to notice a visible object because attention is directed elsewhere.
Correct. The cocktail party effect is the ability to notice personally important information, such as your name, in an unattended conversation.

questions.explanation: The cocktail party effect is the ability to notice personally important information, such as your name, in an unattended conversation.

options.why: Correct. A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

options.why: The table reports group averages, not individual scores.

questions.explanation: A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: A blow to the very back of the head makes a person see flashes of light. Which lobes were affected?

options.why: The somatosensory cortex is the strip at the front of the parietal lobes that registers touch and body sensations.
The prefrontal cortex is the front part of the frontal lobes, which handles executive functions such as planning and self-control.
Correct. The occipital lobes is the lobes at the back of the head, which process visual information.
The frontal lobes is the lobes behind the forehead, which handle planning, judgment and voluntary movement.

questions.explanation: The occipital lobes is the lobes at the back of the head, which process visual information.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.
This is the statistic, not a variable.
Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as persistently high blood pressure, which is made more likely by chronic stress?

options.why: Emotion-focused coping is the reducing of stress by managing one's emotional reaction rather than the stressor.
Immune suppression is the weakening of the body's defenses against illness during long-term stress.
Problem-focused coping is the reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it.
Correct. Hypertension is persistently high blood pressure, which is made more likely by chronic stress.

questions.explanation: Hypertension is persistently high blood pressure, which is made more likely by chronic stress.

questions.stem: A toddler who knows the word 'dog' sees a cow for the first time and calls it a dog. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: A prototype is the best or most typical example of a category.
A concept is a mental grouping of similar objects, events, ideas or people.
Correct. Assimilation is the interpretation of a new experience in terms of an existing schema.
A schema is a mental framework that organizes and interprets information.

questions.explanation: Assimilation is the interpretation of a new experience in terms of an existing schema.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes permissive parenting?

options.text: The parenting style that makes few demands and sets few limits
options.why: Correct. This is what permissive parenting means.

options.text: A person's characteristic emotional reactivity and intensity, which appears early in life
options.why: That describes temperament.

options.text: The parenting style that sets strict rules and expects obedience, with little warmth or discussion
options.why: That describes authoritarian parenting.

options.text: The parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm
options.why: That describes authoritative parenting.

questions.explanation: Permissive parenting is the parenting style that makes few demands and sets few limits.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = +0.75. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: The relationship with the negative sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: After being shouted at by her boss, Gia goes home and shouts at her younger brother. Which defense mechanism is this?

options.why: Projection is the defense mechanism of seeing one's own unacceptable impulses in other people.
Denial is the defense mechanism of refusing to accept a painful reality.
Rationalization is the defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior.
Correct. Displacement is the defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one.

questions.explanation: Displacement is the defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one.

questions.stem: After a stroke, Mr. Lee understands what people say but can only produce slow, broken speech. Which area was most likely damaged?

options.why: Wernicke's area is the area in the left temporal lobe that controls language comprehension.
Aphasia is an impairment of language caused by brain damage.
Hemispheric specialization is the tendency for each side of the brain to handle certain functions, such as language in the left hemisphere.
Correct. Broca's area is the area in the left frontal lobe that controls speech production.

questions.explanation: Broca's area is the area in the left frontal lobe that controls speech production.

questions.stem: Years after losing his arm, a man still feels itching in the missing hand. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Kinesthesis is the sense of the position and movement of body parts, based on receptors in muscles and joints.
The gate control theory is the theory that the spinal cord has a gate that can block pain signals or let them pass to the brain.
Correct. Phantom limb sensation is the feeling of pain or touch in a limb that has been amputated.
The vestibular sense is the sense of balance and head position, based on the semicircular canals of the inner ear.

questions.explanation: Phantom limb sensation is the feeling of pain or touch in a limb that has been amputated.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the distortion of a memory by misleading information received after the event?

options.why: Source amnesia is the inability to remember where, when or how a piece of information was learned.
Constructive memory is the building of a memory at retrieval from stored pieces, expectations and later information.
Imagination inflation is the increased confidence that an event happened after repeatedly imagining it.
Correct. The misinformation effect is the distortion of a memory by misleading information received after the event.

questions.explanation: The misinformation effect is the distortion of a memory by misleading information received after the event.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the tendency to believe that people get what they deserve?

options.why: Correct. The just-world phenomenon is the tendency to believe that people get what they deserve.
Discrimination is unjustified negative behavior toward a group and its members.
A stereotype is a generalized belief about a group of people.
An implicit attitude is an attitude that a person holds without being aware of it.

questions.explanation: The just-world phenomenon is the tendency to believe that people get what they deserve.

questions.stem: Under pressure, Ada stays calm, rarely worries and recovers quickly from setbacks. She would score high on which Big Five trait?

options.why: Extraversion is the Big Five trait of being sociable, outgoing and energetic.
Correct. Emotional stability is the Big Five trait of being calm and secure rather than anxious and moody.
Agreeableness is the Big Five trait of being kind, trusting and cooperative.
Openness to experience is the Big Five trait of being imaginative, curious and willing to try new things.

questions.explanation: Emotional stability is the Big Five trait of being calm and secure rather than anxious and moody.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the stable negative charge inside a neuron when it is not firing?

options.why: The refractory period is the brief pause after a neuron fires during which it cannot fire again.
The action potential is the brief electrical charge that travels down the axon when a neuron fires.
Correct. The resting potential is the stable negative charge inside a neuron when it is not firing.
The all-or-nothing principle is the rule that a neuron either fires at full strength or does not fire at all.

questions.explanation: The resting potential is the stable negative charge inside a neuron when it is not firing.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the monocular depth cue in which an object that partly blocks another is seen as closer?

options.why: Texture gradient is the monocular depth cue in which surfaces look smoother and less detailed as they get farther away.
Retinal disparity is the binocular depth cue based on the difference between the images in the two eyes.
Correct. Interposition is the monocular depth cue in which an object that partly blocks another is seen as closer.
Relative size is the monocular depth cue in which the object that casts the smaller image is seen as farther away.

questions.explanation: Interposition is the monocular depth cue in which an object that partly blocks another is seen as closer.

questions.stem: A doctor records a newborn as female on the basis of anatomy and chromosomes. The doctor is recording which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Sex is the biological characteristics, such as chromosomes and anatomy, by which people are classified as male, female or intersex.
A gender role is the set of behaviors that a culture expects of men or of women.
Sexual orientation is the direction of a person's enduring sexual attraction.
Gender is the socially and culturally influenced attitudes, feelings and behaviors that a culture links to being a boy, girl, man or woman.

questions.explanation: Sex is the biological characteristics, such as chromosomes and anatomy, by which people are classified as male, female or intersex.

questions.stem: Seven students took a memory test. Their scores were 6, 5, 10, 20, 7, 6, 2. What is the mean of the scores?

options.why: That is the median.
Correct. Add the scores (56) and divide by 7.
That is the range.
That is the highest score.

questions.explanation: In order, the scores are 2, 5, 6, 6, 7, 10, 20. Add the scores (56) and divide by 7. The one very high score pulls the mean (8) above the median (6), so the distribution is positively skewed.

options.text: A loose band that slopes upward from left to right
options.why: Correct. A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes positive psychology?

options.text: The appreciation of the good things in one's life, the practice of which raises well-being
options.why: That describes gratitude.

options.text: The ability to recover and adapt well after stress or hardship
options.why: That describes resilience.

options.text: The positive character traits, such as kindness or curiosity, that are most central to a particular person
options.why: That describes signature strengths.

options.text: The scientific study of the strengths and conditions that help people and communities thrive
options.why: Correct. This is what positive psychology means.

questions.explanation: Positive psychology is the scientific study of the strengths and conditions that help people and communities thrive.

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of problem-solving skill

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of problem-solving skill.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Problem-solving skill was defined as the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The group that received hints solved more new puzzles. On average, the value was 7.2 for the group that received hints and 4.6 for the group that practiced alone, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent and assent: parents consented and each child agreed to take part. (Also acceptable: approval by an institutional review board; the right to withdraw.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 64 five-year-old children from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The group that received hints solved more new puzzles. (7.2 compared with 4.6).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that help from an adult affects problem-solving skill. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to help from an adult. The finding illustrates scaffolding within the zone of proximal development: temporary support lets a child master what they could not yet do alone.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Which study methods lead to the best long-term learning?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Spacing study sessions and testing oneself lead to better long-term learning than cramming or rereading.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, students who spread their study over six days recalled 27 of 40 words a month later, compared with 16 for students who studied in one session.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through the spacing effect: distributed practice gives repeated chances to encode and consolidate the material, so it is retained longer than with massed practice.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, students who took practice quizzes scored 68 percent a week later, compared with 49 percent for students who reread the passage.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through the testing effect: retrieving information from memory strengthens the memory and its retrieval cues more than rereading does.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
